LESSON: SIGN READING 4.2.1 FLUENCY

Grade: SNE  /  hearing-impairment / Grade two
Subject: ENGLISH LANGUAGE ACTIVITIES
Strand: Strand 4
Topic 4.2: Sign Reading 4.2.1 Fluency
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 2

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Sign Reading 4.2.1 Fluency, part of Strand 4 in SNE  /  hearing-impairment / Grade two ENGLISH LANGUAGE ACTIVITIES.

Key inquiry question: Why should we pronounce words and articulate signs with correct mouth movement with fingerspelt letter sounds correctly?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

Follow your teacher’s guidance for group work, discussion, and practice on this topic.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Sign Reading 4.2.1 Fluency together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
● Learning to learn: Learning independently as the learner practices sign reading fluently on their own.

● Digital literacy: Interacting with digital devices as the learner sign reads digital texts.

47

Values:
Unity: Learner cooperates with others as they collaborate with peers in groups to practise sign reading.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
Life skills: Effective communication is enhanced as learners acquire sign reading fluency skills.

Link to other learning areas:

Learner is able to relate Sign reading skills to their learning in Kiswahili Language Activities, Religious activities, Mathematical Activities,

Environmental Activities.

Suggested Learning Resources

Adapted course book, Chart, class readers, course books, flash cards, recording devices e.g tablets, mobile phone, dictionary, internet, signed audio- visual recordings, stopwatch.
